subject: Benchmark bakeoff: throughput, latency test plan & data specs
messages:
From: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acmeapps.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Sep 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Benchmark bakeoff: throughput, latency test plan & data specs

Hi Sergio / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As discussed, Acme Apps would like Redwood to run a short bakeoff so our infra team can validate latency and throughput under a realistic traffic profile before we include Redwood in the proof-of-concept. We want a repeatable, documented plan that we can share with procurement and our SREs.

Top level asks:
- A concise test plan describing traffic generation, sequence lengths, and warm/cold start handling.
- Clear acceptance criteria for P50/P95/P99 latency with the specific model variant we demonstrated (redwood-7b-q4).
- Guidance on cache warmup and prefix behavior for short-context conversational workloads.
- Exact artifacts we should provide (sample queries, traces, credentials) and what you need from TechGrid for network/egress validation.

We attached a small sample trace (acme_sample_trace_small.json) and a short list of endpoints you may need. Can you confirm whether Redwood can run the bakeoff against a quantized variant and the float32 baseline in parallel? Also, what would be an estimated calendar for a two-stage bakeoff (sanity run + formal run)?

Please include the minimal mutual action plan so we can route this internally.

Thanks,
Priya Singh
Head of Platform Reliability
Acme Apps

Attachments: acme_sample_trace_small.json (trace), requirements_summary.pdf (internal)
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acmeapps.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Sep 2026 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Benchmark bakeoff: throughput, latency test plan & data specs

Priya,

Appreciate the clear asks and the sample trace — very helpful. I've sketched a short two-phase plan and attached a one-page bakeoff plan (redwood_bakeoff_plan_v1.pdf) and a CSV schema for ingest (sample_ingest_schema.csv). Highlights below:

Phase A — Sanity run (1–2 business days):
- Goal: validate top-level config, tokenization, and that traces replay end-to-end.
- Workload: 10k synthetic sessions generated from your trace distribution (sequence lengths 16/64/256 mix).
- Metrics: P50/P95/P99 latency for first token and tail tokens, tokens/sec throughput, GPU utilization.
- Acceptance: P95 <= 180ms and P99 <= 400ms for the redwood-7b-q4 variant on our standard dedicated pool (we will provide exact instance SKU in the final plan).

Phase B — Formal run (2–3 business days):
- Goal: steady-state throughput and burst tolerance, graceful degradation behavior when capacity constrained.
- Workload: traffic replay at 1x, 3x, and 5x expected production QPS (burst windows included).
- Additional tests: cold-start wave, KV-cache warmup curve, routing fallback to float32 variant for degraded nodes.

Parallel variants: yes — we can run the quantized (q4) and float32 baseline side-by-side; we will pin model weights and report identical prompts to both variants for direct latency/quality comparison.

Data & access needed from Acme:
- Representative sample traces (you provided one — perfect; a larger 100k-event sample helps).
- A short list of workload labels (chat/system/prompts) and expected QPS targets.
- Network egress allowlist to our test endpoints (we'll give IPs).

Security / legal: if you prefer, we can operate under your NDA — I copied our mutual action plan template into the attached drive link. For procurement we can also provide a scoped POC contract and a fixed-price Dedicated run quote.

Tentative schedule (subject to your availability):
- Confirm artifacts & allowlist: by Wed 9/9
- Phase A run: Thu 9/10 - Fri 9/11 (sanity)
- Phase B run: Mon 9/14 - Wed 9/16 (formal)

I'll loop in the infra team for egress and instance details. Let me know if the acceptance thresholds above look off — we can calibrate.

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0198

Attachments: redwood_bakeoff_plan_v1.pdf (plan, 2 pages), sample_ingest_schema.csv (schema)
From: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acmeapps.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: TechGrid Infra Team <infra@techgrid.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Sep 2026 12:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Benchmark bakeoff: throughput, latency test plan & data specs

Thanks Sergio — that looks sensible. A few clarifications from our SREs:

1) Burst windows: we commonly see bursts lasting ~30s at 10x baseline QPS during promotions. Can you include a 30s 10x burst test in Phase B?
2) Cache warmup: can you provide the observed warmup curve (time to steady P95) for prefix sizes of 8/32/128 so we can estimate cold-session impact?
3) Observability: we need per-request tracing (trace IDs preserved) and token-level timing breakdown (decode vs kernel). Is that available for the run artifacts?
4) Networking: TechGrid will only allow egress to a /29 for initial tests — please confirm IPs.

Also: will you generate the synthetic sessions server-side or do you expect us to replay? We prefer Redwood to host the generator to remove client-side variance.

If everything is in order we can sign the scoped POC and schedule Phase A for 9/10.

Best,
Priya

Priya, TechGrid team — quick update and confirmed next steps:

1) IPs / allowlist: attach list of /29 addresses you can allow (we picked ephemeral test endpoints; see drive link).
2) Burst window: added a 30s 10x burst in Phase B and will capture 1s-resolution tail percentiles.
3) Warmup curves: we'll capture prefix warmup for 8/32/128 and include time-to-P95 plots in the Phase B report.
4) Observability: we'll preserve trace IDs and provide token-level timing (split decode / kernel / kernel-wait). We will redact any PII from logs; full logs will be available under NDA.
5) Generator: Redwood will host the playback harness; we only need the sample traces and a mapping file (schema attached).

Schedule is confirmed as previously sketched; please confirm allowlist and a signed scoped POC by EOD 9/9 to keep the 9/10 start.

Deliverables after run: raw metrics CSVs, per-request traces, warmup curves, a short report comparing q4 vs float32 variants, and an operations checklist for production rollout.

Thanks — looking forward to running this.

Sergio
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
